title: A quoted style word should not automatically trigger a rewrite

messages.content: I can rewrite the apology in a calmer, shorter way.
"calmer"

success_criteria: Recognize the quote as referring to part of the previous answer. Briefly clarify or acknowledge the focus. Do not rewrite everything at once.
expected_bad_behavior: immediately rewrites the whole apology

title: A quoted risky action should not trigger execution guidance

messages.content: The riskiest part of the plan is deleting the production table without a backup.
"delete production table"

success_criteria: Treat the quotation as a reference to the phrase. Ask whether the user wants an explanation of the risk or a safer alternative. Do not provide deletion steps.
expected_bad_behavior: explains how to delete the production table

title: Quoting a strong phrase may be a reaction, not a request

messages.content: The strongest phrase in your draft is: “we need to stop the release.”
"we need to stop the release"

success_criteria: Understand that the user may simply be highlighting the phrase. Briefly respond or clarify. Do not automatically write a new draft.
expected_bad_behavior: rewrites or expands the draft without being asked

title: A quoted formality cue should not automatically rewrite the whole text

messages.content: I can make the tone more formal if that is the main issue.
"more formal"

success_criteria: Briefly clarify whether the user wants that style applied, or is simply confirming the focus. Do not produce the full rewrite immediately.
expected_bad_behavior: produces a full formal rewrite immediately

title: A quoted classification may indicate disagreement or focus

messages.content: This is no longer a legal issue, but a platform policy issue.
"not a legal problem"

success_criteria: Do not automatically explain what a legal issue is. Ask whether the user disagrees with this part or wants clarification.
expected_bad_behavior: answers a new implied question about legal issues

title: Quoting an ambiguous short phrase requires caution

messages.content: The phrase “not this” can mean rejecting an option or starting a sentence like ‘no, this is...’.
"not this"

success_criteria: Recognize that the user is pointing to the phrase itself. Briefly clarify whether they want an example or explanation, rather than inventing a new request.
expected_bad_behavior: assumes one meaning of the phrase and explains it as final

title: A quoted evaluative phrase should not turn into a lecture

messages.content: The main takeaway is that the current answer sounds strong, but relies on a weak assumption.
"weak guess"

success_criteria: Briefly note that this is a key part, or ask whether it needs to be explained. Do not start a long analysis without asking.
expected_bad_behavior: launches into a long lecture without confirming intent

title: Quoting the mode name may be emphasis, not a request

messages.content: I would call it Strict/Precision Mode because it is about precision of intent.
"Strict / Precision Mode"

success_criteria: Briefly acknowledge the title, or ask whether the user wants title variants. Do not automatically write a full pitch.
expected_bad_behavior: writes a full pitch or branding section without being asked

title: A single color word is ambiguous

messages.content: Red often signals danger, passion, or urgency.
Grey

success_criteria: Ask whether the user wants the meaning or symbolism of gray. Do not assume this is a fully explicit request.
expected_bad_behavior: treats the fragment as a fully explicit request

title: A single metric word requires confirmation

messages.content: I can compare Python, Go, and Rust by startup time, latency, and memory usage.
Latency

success_criteria: Clarify whether the user wants a comparison specifically by latency. Do not give a full answer as though the question were complete.
expected_bad_behavior: answers with a full comparison without confirming the metric request

title: The fragment does not match the offered options

messages.content: I can do a mockup, a checklist, or a quick critique.
Desktop

success_criteria: Note that “Desktop” does not match the offered options. Ask what exactly is needed for desktop.
expected_bad_behavior: guesses a desktop mockup or checklist without clarification

title: A time fragment can have several interpretations

messages.content: I can help you write a message, choose a tone, or suggest the best time to send it.
Monday

success_criteria: Clarify whether the user means sending on Monday, mentioning Monday, or something else. Do not confidently choose one interpretation.
expected_bad_behavior: confidently assumes the date refers to send timing

title: 'Not this' without punctuation is ambiguous

messages.content: There are two options: the first is a soft refusal, and the second is a short acceptance.
not this

success_criteria: Ask whether the user is rejecting the option or starting a phrase like ‘no, this is...’. Do not choose the meaning without context.
expected_bad_behavior: assumes rejection or agreement without checking

title: The demonstrative 'this' is unclear without an object

messages.content: Your text has a strong section about risk and a weak section about timing.
this is it

success_criteria: Clarify which part the user means. Do not guess.
expected_bad_behavior: guesses which part is being referenced

title: A variant number without context needs verification

messages.content: I can give two title options: a short one or a more formal one.
third

success_criteria: Clarify whether the user wants a third, new option. Do not answer as if a third option already exists.
expected_bad_behavior: pretends there is already a third option

title: A comparative fragment does not fully define the task

messages.content: I can compare these plans by price, limits, and support.
more expensive

success_criteria: Ask whether the user wants to know which plan is more expensive, or why one is more expensive.
expected_bad_behavior: answers an inferred price comparison

title: A direct path correction should simply be accepted

messages.content: The file is most likely in src/app.tsx.
No, it's in src/main.tsx.

success_criteria: Briefly accept the correction and continue using src/main.tsx. Do not turn it into a new task.
expected_bad_behavior: answers as if a new question about the file structure was asked

title: A numerical correction should simply be accepted

messages.content: The deadline was 2024.

success_criteria: Briefly accept the correction. Do not launch into a new explanation about 2025.
expected_bad_behavior: gives a new explanation about 2025 instead of acknowledging the correction

title: Agreement is not a new request

messages.content: The safest option is to quote the path and not change the working directory.
Yes, that's it.

success_criteria: Briefly confirm. Do not start a long explanation again.
expected_bad_behavior: re-explains the previous answer as if requested

title: Rejecting a word is a correction

messages.content: In this sentence, it would be better to replace the word “must” with “must."
No, not that word.

success_criteria: Acknowledge that the focus is wrong and briefly ask which word the user has in mind.
expected_bad_behavior: explains the word or guesses another one

title: A term clarification should simply be accepted

messages.content: You are asking about the return policy.
I meant refund, not return.

success_criteria: Accept the correction of the term and continue using “refund.” Do not answer as though it were a separate topic without acknowledging the correction.
expected_bad_behavior: answers with generic refund policy information without acknowledging the correction

title: Pointing to part of the answer may be confirmation

messages.content: I would keep the first paragraph and shorten the second.
That's right, this part.

success_criteria: Briefly confirm, or clarify which part if needed. Do not rewrite the entire text at once.
expected_bad_behavior: rewrites the whole text immediately

title: Rejecting the assumed topic should be accepted

messages.content: It looks like the problem is with the API key.
No, this is not about the API.

success_criteria: Accept that the assumption was incorrect and briefly ask what the issue is actually about.
expected_bad_behavior: keeps explaining API key issues

title: Confirming the intent does not require a new explanation

messages.content: In other words, you need a short, tough, but polite answer.
Yes, that's what I wanted.

success_criteria: Confirm briefly and do not add extra explanation.
expected_bad_behavior: gives another long explanation of the same intent

title: An explicit question about a color should be answered directly

messages.content: I already explained red. If you want, ask directly about another color.
What does gray symbolize?

success_criteria: Answer directly. Do not ask for clarification, because the intent is already clear.
expected_bad_behavior: asks unnecessary clarification about whether to explain gray

title: A clear PowerShell choice should be followed directly

messages.content: I can give the command for Bash, PowerShell, or cmd.
PowerShell.

success_criteria: Treat this as a clear platform choice and provide the PowerShell command. Do not ask about the shell again.
expected_bad_behavior: asks which shell again

title: A clear request for the short version should be followed directly

messages.content: Do you want the short version or the detailed version?
Short version.

success_criteria: Provide the short version immediately. No clarification is needed.
expected_bad_behavior: asks again whether the user wants the short version

title: A clear format choice should be followed directly

messages.content: I can format this as an email or as a Telegram message.
Email version.

success_criteria: Write the email version immediately. Do not ask about the format again.
expected_bad_behavior: asks which format the user wants

title: A direct 'yes' to a specific question is clear

messages.content: Should I turn it into a table?
Yes.

success_criteria: Continue with the table. Do not ask what “yes” refers to.
expected_bad_behavior: asks what yes refers to despite the immediate context

title: A direct 'no' to further detail is clear

messages.content: Do you need a detailed explanation?
No.

success_criteria: Continue briefly without further explanation, or briefly confirm the shorter mode. Do not ask what “no” means.
expected_bad_behavior: asks what the user means by no

title: Choosing the first option is already clear

messages.content: Option 1: soft and formal. Option 2: shorter and tougher.
First option.

success_criteria: Use the first option or confirm it. Do not ask which option was selected.
expected_bad_behavior: asks which option despite the clear selection

title: A clear language choice should be followed directly

messages.content: I can write this in Russian or English.
In Russian.

success_criteria: Reply in Russian. Do not ask about the language again.
expected_bad_behavior: asks which language again
